method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of Macfarlane et al., Australian Prescriber 2026;49(1), published 10 February 2026, including Box 1 (definitions) and Box 2 (the eight quality statements of the ACSQHC Psychotropic Medicines in Cognitive Disability or Impairment Clinical Care Standard, reproduced there). No drug-level recommendation, dose or PRN rule is asserted; those sit in the 2023 Australian clinical practice guideline (Bell et al.), which was not retrieved. Author conflicts of interest are declared in the source and noted in the guideline.

claims.claim: Royal Commissions into the aged-care and disability sectors revealed significant concerns about the inappropriate use of psychotropic medicines as chemical restraint in people with cognitive disability or impairment
claims.source_text: Royal Commissions into the aged-care and disability sectors revealed significant concerns about the inappropriate use of psychotropic medicines as chemical restraint in people with cognitive disability or impairment.

claims.claim: The Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety and the Royal Commission into Violence, Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of People with Disability highlighted the extent to which inappropriate prescribing of psychotropic medicines was occurring, especially antipsychotic medicines such as risperidone and quetiapine and anxiolytic or hypnotic medicines mostly benzodiazepines such as diazepam and oxazepam
claims.source_text: the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety, and the Royal Commission into Violence, Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of People with Disability, highlighted the extent to which inappropriate prescribing of psychotropic medicines was occurring in the aged-care and disability sectors in Australia, especially antipsychotic medicines (e.g. risperidone, quetiapine) and anxiolytic or hypnotic medicines (mostly benzodiazepines such as diazepam, oxazepam).

claims.claim: In aged care the issue primarily related to overuse of psychotropic medicines for people with behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia, whereas in the disability sector it related to psychotropic management of behaviours of concern largely in the context of non-progressive cognitive disability
claims.source_text: In aged care, the issue primarily related to the overuse of psychotropic medicines for people with behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD), whereas in the disability sector it related to psychotropic management of behaviours of concern largely in the context of non-progressive cognitive disability.

claims.claim: Concerns had existed for many years with high rates and considerable variation in prescribing reported
claims.source_text: concerns had existed for many years, with high rates and considerable variation in prescribing reported.

claims.claim: The Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care developed the Psychotropic Medicines in Cognitive Disability or Impairment Clinical Care Standard in consultation with the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission and the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission
claims.source_text: the Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care developed the Psychotropic Medicines in Cognitive Disability or Impairment Clinical Care Standard (the Standard) in consultation with the NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) Quality and Safeguards Commission and the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission.

claims.claim: Use of psychotropic medicines for behaviours of concern is regarded by legislation as chemical restraint, which is a type of restrictive practice defined as the use of a medicine or chemical substance for the primary purpose of influencing a person's behaviour
claims.source_text: Use of psychotropic medicines in this context is regarded by legislation as chemical restraint, which is a type of restrictive practice defined as the use of a medicine or chemical substance for the primary purpose of influencing a person's (or care recipient's) behaviour

claims.claim: There are five restrictive practices subject to regulation and oversight under the NDIS Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support Rules 2018 and the Aged Care Act 2024 and Aged Care Rules 2025: chemical restraint, environmental restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint and seclusion
claims.source_text: There are 5 restrictive practices that are subject to regulation and oversight under the NDIS (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018, and the Aged Care Act 2024 and Aged Care Rules 2025: chemical restraint; environmental restraint; mechanical restraint; physical restraint; seclusion.

claims.claim: The use of restrictive practices in Australia is also subject to state and territory legislation
claims.source_text: The use of restrictive practices in Australia is also subject to state and territory legislation.

claims.claim: The definition of chemical restraint specifically excludes medicines prescribed for the treatment of a mental or physical illness or condition including end-of-life care, and also excludes medicines used to support access to necessary medical appointments or investigations such as a benzodiazepine administered before a blood test or imaging procedure, because psychotropic medicines are used for a broad range of therapeutic purposes and clearly not all psychotropic use equates to chemical restraint
claims.source_text: This definition specifically excludes the use of medicines prescribed for the treatment of a mental or physical illness or condition, including end-of-life care. It also excludes medicines used to support access to necessary medical appointments or investigations, such as when a benzodiazepine is administered before a blood test or imaging procedure. These are important exclusions, as psychotropic medicines are used for a broad range of therapeutic purposes, and clearly not all psychotropic use equates to chemical restraint.

claims.claim: The Standard focuses predominantly on three psychotropic medicine groups, antidepressants, antipsychotics and anxiolytics or hypnotics, however use of other medicines such as anticonvulsants for the primary purpose of influencing a person's behaviour would also be considered chemical restraint
claims.source_text: The Standard focuses predominantly on 3 psychotropic medicine groups: antidepressants, antipsychotics, and anxiolytics/hypnotics. However use of other medicines (e.g. anticonvulsants) for the primary purpose of influencing a person's behaviour would also be considered chemical restraint.

claims.claim: Behaviours of concern are behaviours that indicate a risk to the safety or wellbeing of the person who exhibits them or those around them, may serve a purpose for the person such as communicating unmet needs or responding to their environment, and behaviours that cause concern to others may not be concerning to the person who exhibits them
claims.source_text: Behaviours that indicate a risk to the safety or wellbeing of the person who exhibits them, or the safety or wellbeing of those around them. Behaviours may challenge the person, their supporters and the care services they are in, but may serve a purpose for the person, such as communicating unmet needs or responding to their environment. Behaviours that cause concern to others may not be concerning to the person who exhibits them.

claims.claim: A behaviour support plan is a written plan prepared with the person and their family or support people as appropriate that helps those involved in the person's daily life and care to improve the person's care, reduce or prevent behaviours of concern, and potentially eliminate the need for restrictive practices to control behaviour
claims.source_text: A written plan, prepared with the person (and their family or support people as appropriate), that helps those involved in the person's daily life and care to improve the person's care, reduce or prevent behaviours of concern, and potentially eliminate the need for restrictive practices to control behaviour.

claims.claim: Best-practice management of behaviours of concern comprises an initial thorough assessment to identify and manage underlying causes, followed by discussion with the patient, family and caregivers, non-medication management and problem-solving approaches, environmental approaches and adaptations with a tailored activity program, and last in the process if these are not adequate a stepped trial of medicines
claims.source_text: Best-practice management of behaviours of concern in both aged and disability care is broadly agreed to comprise an initial thorough assessment to enable identification and management of any underlying causes of behaviour change. This is followed by discussion with the patient, their family and caregivers about the issues, and providing them with non-medication management (e.g. behavioural strategies) and problem-solving approaches. Environmental approaches and adaptations, in conjunction with a tailored activity program, are also important. Last in the process, if the above approaches are not adequate, is a stepped trial of medicines.

claims.claim: It is good practice and a regulatory requirement for both the aged-care and disability sectors to develop and implement an individual behaviour support plan for a person with behaviours of concern, and psychotropic medicines and other types of restrictive practice must be a last resort following consideration and use of alternative strategies which must be detailed in the behaviour support plan
claims.source_text: It is good practice, and a regulatory requirement for both the aged-care and disability sectors, to develop and implement an individual behaviour support plan for a person with behaviours of concern. Psychotropic medicines and other types of restrictive practice for behaviours of concern must be a last resort following consideration and use of alternative strategies which must be detailed in the behaviour support plan.

claims.claim: Medical practitioners need to independently obtain informed consent from either their patient or their patient's legally appointed medical decision-maker prior to the use of restricted practice including the prescription of a medicine, and where there is no person authorised under relevant jurisdictional legislation to provide consent, escalation through the relevant state or territory specific authorising body is required
claims.source_text: Medical practitioners need to independently obtain informed consent from either their patient or their patient's legally appointed medical decision-maker prior to the use of restricted practice, including the prescription of a medicine. Where there is no person who is authorised under relevant jurisdictional legislation to provide consent, escalation through the relevant state- or territory-specific authorising body is required.

claims.claim: Aged-care and disability providers have additional requirements under their regulatory frameworks for authorisation of restrictive practice including ensuring informed consent has been obtained by the prescriber, and for monitoring and reporting the use of chemical restraint to the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission and the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission respectively
claims.source_text: Aged-care and disability providers have additional requirements under their regulatory frameworks for authorisation of restrictive practice (including ensuring informed consent has been obtained by the prescriber), and for monitoring and reporting the use of chemical restraint to the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission and the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission respectively.

claims.claim: While regulatory frameworks are legally binding on aged-care and disability service providers they are not binding upon individual prescribers who provide medical services within service providers' facilities or in general practice, other specialist clinics and hospitals, and service providers and prescribers may therefore approach behaviour management from different perspectives leading to challenges in coordinating inputs into approval processes
claims.source_text: While regulatory frameworks are legally binding on aged-care and disability service providers, they are not binding upon individual prescribers who provide medical services either within service providers' facilities (such as general practitioners and nurse practitioners) or in general practice, other specialist clinics and hospitals. Service providers and prescribers may therefore approach behaviour management from different perspectives, leading to challenges in coordinating inputs into approval processes.

claims.claim: In practice this places prescribers in a situation of needing to support service providers with authorisation and document the reason for chemical restraint
claims.source_text: In practice, this places prescribers in a situation of needing to support service providers with authorisation and document the reason for chemical restraint.

claims.claim: The Standard emphasises that clinicians should only consider prescribing psychotropic medicines to influence behaviour if the behaviours either pose a substantial risk to the person or to others or are significantly reducing the person's quality of life, and emergency use is also justified if such use can facilitate necessary clinical assessments or interventions
claims.source_text: The Standard emphasises that clinicians should only consider prescribing psychotropic medicines to influence behaviour if the behaviours either pose a substantial risk to the person or to others, or are significantly reducing the person's quality of life. Emergency use is also justified if such use can facilitate necessary clinical assessments or interventions.

claims.claim: Not all behaviours of concern respond to psychotropic medicines, for example antipsychotic drugs are usually not effective for reducing calling out, disinhibition, wandering and exit-seeking, but they may reduce agitation and aggression
claims.source_text: It is important to be aware that not all behaviours of concern respond to psychotropic medicines (e.g. antipsychotic drugs are usually not effective for reducing calling out, disinhibition, wandering and exit-seeking, but they may reduce agitation and aggression).

claims.claim: The Standard encourages service providers to have clear policies in place around psychotropic use including the need for documentation of non-medication strategies trialled before such use and for monitoring of the effectiveness of any psychotropic prescribed
claims.source_text: The Standard encourages service providers to have clear policies in place around psychotropic use, including the need for documentation of non-medication strategies trialled before such use, and for monitoring of the effectiveness of any psychotropic prescribed.

claims.claim: An Australian clinical practice guideline for the appropriate use of psychotropic medicines in people living with dementia and in residential aged care including people with both dementia and intellectual disability was published in 2023, providing recommendations and good practice statements about antipsychotics, benzodiazepines and antidepressants with respect to their benefits and harms, discontinuation and pro re nata use
claims.source_text: An Australian clinical practice guideline for the appropriate use of psychotropic medicines in people living with dementia and in residential aged care (including people with both dementia and intellectual disability) was published in 2023. This guideline provides recommendations and good practice statements about antipsychotics, benzodiazepines and antidepressants, specifically with respect to their benefits and harms, discontinuation and pro re nata (PRN) use.

claims.claim: Guidance on prescribing psychotropic medicines is more limited for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities due to a paucity of high-quality evidence, with some evidence supporting risperidone and aripiprazole in reducing behaviours of concern in children with intellectual disability and atypical antipsychotics and ADHD medicines in reducing irritability in autism, although side effects are problematic
claims.source_text: Guidance on prescribing psychotropic medicines is more limited for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities due to a paucity of high-quality evidence in this population. Some evidence supports the use of risperidone and aripiprazole in reducing behaviours of concern in children with intellectual disability, and the use of atypical antipsychotics and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medicines in reducing irritability in autism, although side effects are problematic.

claims.claim: Common harms associated with most psychotropic medicines include but are not limited to cognitive impairment, sedation and increased risk of falls
claims.source_text: Common harms associated with most psychotropic medicines include, but are not limited to, cognitive impairment, sedation and increased risk of falls.

claims.claim: Adverse effects associated with antipsychotic medicines include extrapyramidal side effects, weight gain, increased cardiovascular risk and, in people with dementia, increased risk of cerebrovascular events and death
claims.source_text: Adverse effects associated with antipsychotic medicines include extrapyramidal side effects, weight gain, increased cardiovascular risk, and, in people with dementia, increased risk of cerebrovascular events and death.

claims.claim: Agitation and irritability are the behaviours most commonly leading to referral to Dementia Support Australia and account for much of the inappropriate prescribing that occurs in people with dementia
claims.source_text: Agitation and irritability are the behaviours most commonly leading to referral to Dementia Support Australia (Dementia Support Australia, unpublished data) and account for much of the inappropriate prescribing that occurs in people with dementia.

claims.claim: Despite fears that behaviours of concern may re-emerge if psychotropics are stopped, many behaviours such as agitation and irritability are relatively transient and self-limiting
claims.source_text: Despite fears that behaviours of concern may re-emerge if psychotropics are stopped, many behaviours such as agitation and irritability are relatively transient and self-limiting.

claims.claim: It is common for psychotropic medicines to be continued long term, with one Australian study reporting usage for an average of 2.2 years, despite the risks from longer term use being well known
claims.source_text: It is common for psychotropic medicines to be continued long term (e.g. one Australian study reported usage for an average of 2.2 years), despite the risks from longer term use being well known.

claims.claim: Many older people who have had antipsychotics initiated in hospital for short-term management of behaviours of concern have them continued upon discharge
claims.source_text: Many older people who have had antipsychotics initiated in hospital for short-term management of behaviours of concern have them continued upon discharge.

claims.claim: For people with cognitive disabilities psychotropic medicines are frequently prescribed to manage behaviours of concern in the absence of a diagnosed mental illness and their ongoing use may no longer be appropriate as circumstances evolve or once behavioural and environmental strategies have taken effect
claims.source_text: For people with cognitive disabilities, including those with intellectual and developmental disabilities, psychotropic medicines are frequently prescribed to manage behaviours of concern in the absence of a diagnosed mental illness, and their ongoing use may no longer be appropriate as circumstances evolve, or once behavioural and environmental strategies have taken effect.

claims.claim: Psychotropic polypharmacy is common in this population and should be rationalised and minimised wherever possible, and people with intellectual and developmental disabilities have varying abilities to recognise and communicate adverse effects necessitating proactive and vigilant monitoring
claims.source_text: Psychotropic polypharmacy is common in this population and should be rationalised and minimised wherever possible. People with intellectual and developmental disabilities have varying abilities to recognise and communicate adverse effects, necessitating proactive and vigilant monitoring.

claims.claim: The frequency of review should be guided by the context of use, the medicine and clinical need, typically more frequently during initiation and dose changes and whenever there are new behaviours, emerging adverse effects, or changes in health or circumstances
claims.source_text: The frequency of review should be guided by the context of use, the medicine, and clinical need - typically more frequently during initiation and dose changes, and whenever there are new behaviours, emerging adverse effects, or changes in health or circumstances.

claims.claim: The Standard highlights the need to consider the potential for dose reduction or stopping psychotropic medicines at each review taking into account whether behaviours have stabilised and adverse effects have emerged, and if behaviours have been settled for 3 months or more at review the need for ongoing use should be assessed
claims.source_text: The Standard highlights the need to consider the potential for dose reduction or stopping psychotropic medicines (deprescribing) at each review, taking into account whether behaviours have stabilised and adverse effects have emerged. If behaviours have been settled for 3 months or more at review, the need for ongoing use should be assessed.

claims.claim: Involving the person's family or support network in the review process facilitates shared decision-making, and clear documentation of review outcomes including the rationale for continuing, changing or stopping medication is important for continuity of care
claims.source_text: Involving the person's family or support network in the review process facilitates shared decision-making; and clear documentation of review outcomes - including the rationale for continuing, changing or stopping medication - is important for continuity of care.

claims.claim: Stopping a psychotropic medicine should usually be undertaken slowly using an individualised tapering plan to reduce the risk of discontinuation symptoms
claims.source_text: Stopping a psychotropic medicine should usually be undertaken slowly using an individualised tapering plan to reduce the risk of discontinuation symptoms.

claims.claim: Ideally a plan for deprescribing should be made when the medicine is started, and as a minimum the expected duration of therapy should be communicated to the patient and those involved in their care
claims.source_text: Ideally, a plan for deprescribing should be made when the medicine is started; as a minimum, the expected duration of therapy should be communicated to the patient and those involved in their care.

claims.claim: The Australian Deprescribing Network provides a gateway to local and international resources to support and guide deprescribing for a range of medications including psychotropic medicines
claims.source_text: The Australian Deprescribing Network provides a gateway to local and international resources to support and guide deprescribing for a range of medications, including psychotropic medicines.

claims.claim: Transitions of care are associated with risk of medication errors and adverse events, and aged-care and disability providers must ensure that up-to-date behavioural data, medication lists, medical histories and contact details of key people in the person's support network are available at clinical appointments and transfers to hospital
claims.source_text: Transitions of care are associated with risk of medication errors and adverse events. ... Aged-care and disability providers must ensure that up-to-date behavioural data, medication lists, medical histories and contact details of key people in the person's support network are available at clinical appointments and transfers to hospital.

claims.claim: Whenever psychotropic medicines are prescribed clinical communications should include the rationale for medication initiation, target symptoms, evidence of effectiveness, potential and observed adverse effects, reasons for any medication changes, and recommendations for duration of therapy and ongoing monitoring
claims.source_text: whenever psychotropic medicines are prescribed, clinical communications should include the rationale for medication initiation, target symptoms, evidence of effectiveness, potential and observed adverse effects, reasons for any medication changes, and recommendations for duration of therapy and ongoing monitoring.

claims.claim: Among people discharged from hospital with a psychotropic medicine for behaviours associated with dementia or other cognitive disturbance very few are provided with a psychotropic management plan, and providing a plan for reviewing and stopping the psychotropic medicine is an important step to prevent long-term inappropriate use
claims.source_text: Among people discharged from hospital with a psychotropic medicine for behaviours associated with dementia or other cognitive disturbance, very few are provided with a psychotropic management plan. Providing a plan for reviewing and stopping the psychotropic medicine is an important step to prevent long-term inappropriate use.

claims.claim: Quality statement 1 Person-centred care states that a person receives health care driven by their individual preferences, needs and values that upholds their personal dignity, human rights and legal rights, and that the person is supported to be an active participant in making informed choices about their care together with their family, support people or nominated decision-maker as appropriate
claims.source_text: A person receives health care that is driven by their individual preferences, needs and values, and that upholds their personal dignity, human rights and legal rights. The person is supported to be an active participant in making informed choices about their care, together with their family, support people or nominated decision-maker as appropriate.

claims.claim: Quality statement 2 Informed consent states that if psychotropic medicines are being considered the person and their family, support people or nominated decision-maker as appropriate is informed about the reason, intended duration and potential benefits and harms of treatment, that if use is agreed informed consent is documented before use, and that in an emergency or if the person does not have capacity to make a decision even with support, processes are followed in accordance with relevant legislation
claims.source_text: If psychotropic medicines are being considered, the person - and their family, support people or nominated decision-maker as appropriate - is informed about the reason, intended duration, and potential benefits and harms of treatment. If use of a psychotropic medicine is agreed, informed consent is documented before use. In an emergency, or if the person does not have capacity to make a decision even with support, processes are followed in accordance with relevant legislation.

claims.claim: Quality statement 3 Assessing behaviours states that a person with behaviours of concern is initially assessed for immediate risks to their safety and others, is further assessed to identify clinical, psychosocial and environmental causes of the behaviours and to understand the context in which they occur, and that assessment is carried out by suitably trained individuals and considers existing plans to support the person's care and information from others who know the person well
claims.source_text: A person with behaviours of concern is initially assessed for immediate risks to their safety and others. The person is further assessed to identify clinical, psychosocial and environmental causes of the behaviours, and to understand the context in which they occur. Assessment is carried out by suitably trained individuals, and considers existing plans to support the person's care and information from others who know the person well.

claims.claim: Quality statement 4 Non-medication strategies states that non-medication strategies are used first line and as the mainstay of care when responding to behaviours of concern, and that the choice of strategies is individualised to the person and is documented and communicated to all those involved in their care
claims.source_text: Non-medication strategies are used first line and as the mainstay of care when responding to behaviours of concern. The choice of strategies is individualised to the person, and is documented and communicated to all those involved in their care.

claims.claim: Quality statement 5 Behaviour support plans states that if a person has a plan to support their behaviour it is used to inform and support their care, and that the person's response to care provided under the plan including any use of psychotropic medicines is continually assessed, documented and communicated to inform regular updates to the plan and prescribing decisions
claims.source_text: If a person has a plan to support their behaviour, it is used to inform and support their care. The person's response to care provided under the plan - including any use of psychotropic medicines - is continually assessed, documented and communicated to inform regular updates to the plan and prescribing decisions.

claims.claim: Quality statement 6 Appropriate reasons for prescribing states that psychotropic medicines are considered in response to behaviours only when there is a significant risk of harm to the person or others or when the behaviours have a major impact on the person's quality of life and a reasonable trial of non-medication strategies has been ineffective, that psychotropic medicines are also considered when a mental health condition has been diagnosed or is reasonably suspected following a documented clinical assessment, and that the reason for use is clearly documented in the person's healthcare record at the time of prescribing
claims.source_text: Psychotropic medicines are considered in response to behaviours only when there is a significant risk of harm to the person or others, or when the behaviours have a major impact on the person's quality of life and a reasonable trial of non-medication strategies has been ineffective. Psychotropic medicines are also considered when a mental health condition has been diagnosed or is reasonably suspected following a documented clinical assessment. The reason for use is clearly documented in the person's healthcare record at the time of prescribing.

claims.claim: Quality statement 7 Monitoring, reviewing and ceasing states that a person's response to psychotropic medicines is regularly monitored and reviewed according to the person's individual needs and goals of treatment, that the benefits and harms of treatment and the potential for dose adjustment or cessation are considered at each review, and that the outcome is documented and communicated along with the timing of the next review
claims.source_text: A person's response to psychotropic medicines is regularly monitored and reviewed according to the person's individual needs and goals of treatment. The benefits and harms of treatment and the potential for dose adjustment or cessation are considered at each review. The outcome is documented and communicated, along with the timing of the next review.

claims.claim: Quality statement 8 Information sharing and communication at transitions of care states that when the health care of a person is transferred, information about their ongoing needs is shared with the person, their family or support people and the healthcare and service providers continuing their care including information about behaviour support plans or other strategies, and that if psychotropic medicines are prescribed the reason for use, intended duration, timing of last administration and plans for monitoring and review are documented and communicated
claims.source_text: When the health care of a person is transferred, information about their ongoing needs is shared with the person, their family or support people and the healthcare and service providers continuing their care. This includes information about behaviour support plans or other strategies. If psychotropic medicines are prescribed, the reason for use, intended duration, timing of last administration, and plans for monitoring and review are documented and communicated to support the person's ongoing care.

claims.claim: The Standard comprises 8 quality statements addressing priority areas where improvements in clinical practice are expected to translate to better health outcomes for people with cognitive disability or impairment, and each quality statement is accompanied by one or more indicators
claims.source_text: The Standard comprises 8 quality statements addressing priority areas where improvements in clinical practice are expected to translate to better health outcomes for people with cognitive disability or impairment. Each quality statement is accompanied by one or more indicators that may be used by clinicians and health service providers to assess and monitor their care practices and to improve them where action is required.

claims.claim: Psychotropic medicines are broadly defined as any medicine that can influence the mind, emotions or behaviour
claims.source_text: Psychotropic medicines are broadly defined as any medicine that can influence the mind, emotions or behaviour.
